title: NT-proBNP and high intensity care for acute heart failure: the STRONG-HF trial.
abstract: In the STRONG-HF trial, a high-intensity post-discharge care strategy with rapid up-titration of guideline-directed medical therapy reduced 180-day heart failure readmission or death compared with usual care, independent of baseline NT-proBNP level.
quality_notes: STRONG-HF RCT published in European Heart Journal (n=1077), testing rapid up-titration of guideline-directed medical therapies with high-intensity follow-up. Landmark trial in a top cardiology journal; rigorous randomization, preregistered outcomes, and safety monitoring. Directly relevant to post-discharge medication management.
screening_rationale: STRONG-HF trial — high-intensity post-discharge care (frequent visits + BNP monitoring + rapid GDMT uptitration) vs. usual care after AHF — care transition intervention with readmission/mortality outcomes
fulltext_rationale: RCT; NT-proBNP-guided high-intensity post-discharge follow-up for acute HF (STRONG-HF); reports readmission
intervention_details: Rapid up-titration of guideline-recommended medical therapy (GRMT) - high intensity care (HIC) strategy with NT-proBNP monitoring (STRONG-HF)

title: Transitional Care Interventions to Prevent Readmissions for Persons With Heart Failure
abstract: This AHRQ-commissioned systematic review and meta-analysis pooled evidence on transitional care interventions for adults with heart failure and found that certain intervention types, particularly those combining home visits with structured follow-up, were associated with reduced readmissions.
quality_notes: AHRQ-commissioned SR/meta-analysis published in Annals of Internal Medicine (2014), among the most rigorous and frequently cited reviews on HF transitional care. Dual independent screening, comprehensive search, formal risk of bias, and GRADE-level evidence synthesis expected per AHRQ standards.
screening_rationale: AHRQ systematic review of transitional care interventions to prevent readmissions for HF — directly on PICO
fulltext_rationale: SR/MA (Feltner 2014); transitional care interventions to prevent HF readmissions; major review
intervention_details: Transitional care interventions for HF (comprehensive AHRQ-funded review)

title: A Randomized Trial of Home Telemonitoring in a Typical Elderly Heart Failure Population in North West London: Results of the Home-HF Study
abstract: The Home-HF trial compared home telemonitoring with usual specialist care in an elderly heart failure population and found similar mortality between groups, with fewer clinic and emergency department visits in the telemonitoring arm.
quality_notes: Eur J Heart Failure RCT (Home-HF Study) of home telemonitoring in typical elderly HF population in North West London. High-quality cardiology journal; elderly real-world population enhances generalizability. Randomized design with telemonitoring vs usual care comparison.
screening_rationale: Home-HF Study RCT — home telemonitoring in elderly HF patients vs. usual specialist care; reports hospitalization and clinic visit outcomes
fulltext_rationale: RCT; home telemonitoring in elderly HF population (Home-HF study); reports readmission/mortality
intervention_details: Home telemonitoring for typical elderly HF population in North West London (Home-HF study)
author_conclusions: Home telemonitoring achieved similar mortality outcomes to usual specialist care while reducing clinic and emergency visits.

title: Post-discharge Follow-up Characteristics Associated With 30-Day Readmission After Heart Failure Hospitalization
abstract: This registry-based cohort study of heart failure patients discharged home evaluated how soon and with which type of clinician patients were seen after discharge, and reported that earlier physician follow-up related to a reduced risk of readmission within 30 days.
quality_notes: Medical Care prospective cohort on post-discharge follow-up characteristics and 30-day readmissions. High-impact health services journal; specific analysis of follow-up type and timing relevant for program design. Registry-based design captures real-world patterns.
screening_rationale: Post-discharge follow-up characteristics and 30-day readmission in HF — outpatient follow-up within 7 days as care transition intervention with readmission outcome
fulltext_rationale: Prospective cohort; post-discharge follow-up characteristics and 30-day HF readmission
intervention_details: Post-discharge follow-up with cardiology or general medicine provider within 7 days of HF hospitalization
comparison_details: No follow-up or follow-up after 7 days
author_conclusions: Seeing a physician soon after discharge was linked to a lower 30-day readmission risk.

title: Remote Monitoring of Patients With Heart Failure: An Overview of Systematic Reviews
abstract: This umbrella review pooled findings from earlier systematic reviews of remote-monitoring approaches in heart failure, reporting that the supporting evidence was strongest for established monitoring programs and less certain for newer app- and video-based methods.
quality_notes: Overview of systematic reviews (umbrella review) in JMIR on telemonitoring, examining both structured telemonitoring and non-invasive remote monitoring modalities. JMIR applies rigorous methodological standards; appropriate design for synthesizing existing SR evidence.
screening_rationale: Overview of SRs on remote monitoring for HF — telemonitoring and home telehealth with rehospitalization and mortality outcomes; umbrella review
fulltext_rationale: Overview of systematic reviews; remote monitoring for HF; synthesizes readmission evidence
intervention_details: Remote monitoring for HF including telemonitoring, home telehealth, mobile phone monitoring, and videoconferencing
author_conclusions: Evidence was most supportive of established remote-monitoring programs, with newer digital approaches still requiring study.

title: Reducing rehospitalization in cardiac patients: a randomized, controlled trial of a cardiac care management program ("Cardiolotse") in Germany.
abstract: In a multicenter randomized controlled trial in Germany, a cardiac care navigator program providing post-discharge support to cardiac patients (Cardiolotse) reduced the rate and length of all-cause rehospitalization compared with standard care.
quality_notes: Large multicenter RCT (n=2862, Cardiolotse) published in BMC Medicine. Large sample with adequate power; pragmatic design enhances real-world applicability. Cardiac care management model (coordinator-based) directly relevant to hospital transition programs.
screening_rationale: Cardiolotse RCT — cardiac care navigator post-discharge for rehospitalization reduction — directly on PICO
fulltext_rationale: RCT; cardiac care management program (Cardiolotse) for cardiac patients including HF; reports rehospitalization
intervention_details: Cardiac care management program Cardiolotse: cardiac care navigators providing post-discharge support for HF, CAD, and arrhythmia patients
